ai.name: Artificial Intelligence
ai.description: The end-to-end AI value chain — from the materials and tools that make chips, through compute, memory, networking, power and cooling, up to the clouds and software that sell AI.

links.name: Materials & Inputs
links.what: The raw stuff of chips: ultra-pure silicon wafers, specialty gases, chemicals and substrates. Boring but essential — nothing gets made without it.

links.name: Chip Design Tools & IP
links.what: The software used to design chips (EDA) and the reusable circuit blueprints (IP). You cannot design a modern chip without these tools.

links.name: Semiconductor Equipment
links.what: The machines that actually etch and build chips inside a factory. A handful of firms make the tools every chipmaker on earth depends on.

members.company: ASML Holding N.V. - New York Re
members.why: Lithography — the machine that prints chips (near-monopoly)
Test & measurement across chip and network design

links.name: AI Compute Silicon (GPUs/Accelerators)
links.what: The chips that do the AI maths — GPUs and custom accelerators. This is the part most people mean when they say "AI stocks."

members.why: The GPU standard for AI training

links.name: Foundries (Manufacturing)
links.what: The factories that physically manufacture the chips others design. Extremely hard and expensive to build; very few companies can do it at the cutting edge.

members.why: Makes most of the world's advanced AI chips

links.name: Memory & Storage (incl. HBM)
links.what: Chips that hold data for the AI to work on. High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) sits right next to the GPU and has become a key bottleneck.

members.why: HBM & DRAM — the key memory bottleneck

links.name: Advanced Packaging & Test
links.what: Stitching multiple chips into one high-performance package, then testing them. As raw chip shrinks slow, packaging is where a lot of the gains now come from.

links.name: Networking & Interconnect
links.what: The switches and high-speed links that connect thousands of GPUs into one giant computer. A data center is only as fast as its slowest connection.

links.name: Optical & Photonics
links.what: Moving data as light — transceivers, lasers and optical fiber. Essential for the huge bandwidth between AI servers.

members.why: RF & photonic components for optical links

links.name: Power Delivery & Electrical
links.what: Getting clean power to the chips: power semiconductors, voltage modules and the electrical gear feeding the rack.

members.why: Power management & signal chain on AI boards
Electrical power management for data centers

links.name: Thermal & Cooling
links.what: AI chips run hot. Liquid cooling and thermal systems keep them from melting — one of the fastest-growing corners of the chain.

members.why: Liquid cooling & data-center thermal (a key winner)

links.name: Servers, Systems & ODMs
links.what: The companies that assemble chips, memory and cooling into finished AI servers and racks.

members.why: ODM / contract manufacturing for AI hardware

links.name: Data-Center Real Estate
links.what: The physical buildings — landlords who own and lease the data centers the clouds fill with AI hardware.

links.name: Power Generation & Grid
links.what: AI is enormously power-hungry. Generators (including nuclear), grid builders and electrical equipment makers supply the electricity.

members.why: Nuclear power — signing deals to power data centers
Builds the electrical grid & data-center power

links.name: Hyperscalers / Cloud (the Buyers)
links.what: The giants that buy most of the AI hardware and rent AI out as a service. Their spending ("capex") drives the whole chain.

members.why: Massive GPU buyer for its own AI

links.name: AI Software, Platforms & Apps
links.what: The models, data platforms and applications that turn AI into products people pay for — the top of the chain.

cyber.name: Cybersecurity
cyber.description: The layers of digital defense — from who gets in (identity) through the devices, network, cloud, data and code, up to the security control room and the people who run it.

links.name: Identity & Access
links.what: Controls who is allowed in — logins, single sign-on, passwords and privileged accounts. The front door of security.

members.why: Entra ID — the biggest identity platform

links.name: Endpoint Protection
links.what: Guards the actual devices — laptops, servers, phones — where attacks land and data lives.

links.name: Network & Firewall
links.what: The walls and gates around the network; inspects the traffic flowing in and out.

links.name: Cloud & App Security
links.what: Secures the cloud apps and infrastructure companies now run everything on.

links.name: Email & Web Security
links.what: Blocks phishing, malicious links and web threats — the most common way attackers get in.

links.name: Data Security & Backup
links.what: Protects and backs up the data itself, so a breach or ransomware attack cannot destroy it.

links.name: Vulnerability & Code Security
links.what: Finds the holes before attackers do — scanning systems and securing software as it is built.

links.name: Detection & Response (SOC)
links.what: The security control room — collects signals from everything and hunts threats in real time.

links.name: Security Services & Consulting
links.what: The people who design, run and respond — managed security providers, consultants and government contractors.

quantum.name: Quantum Computing
quantum.description: The race to build computers that harness quantum physics — from the picks-and-shovels hardware, through the pure-play startups and big-tech giants building the machines, to the "quantum-safe" security layer rising to defend against them and the industries set to benefit first.

links.name: Enabling Hardware
links.what: The picks-and-shovels every quantum computer needs — lasers, photonics, vacuum systems and the cryogenic test gear that keeps qubits near absolute zero.

links.name: Big Tech & Cloud
links.what: The deep-pocketed giants building their own quantum chips and renting quantum access through their clouds — the ones most likely to cross the finish line.

members.why: Google Quantum AI — the Willow chip
Majority owner of Quantinuum — trapped ion (Honeywell)
Quantum roadmap leader + IBM Quantum cloud
CUDA-Q + GPU quantum simulation — the hybrid bridge

links.name: Pure-Play Quantum
links.what: Small, high-risk companies built entirely around quantum — each betting on a different way to build a qubit, with little revenue but huge potential.

members.why: Trapped-ion quantum computers — the largest pure-play (IonQ)

links.name: Quantum-Safe Security
links.what: The flip side: quantum computers could one day crack today's encryption, so a whole "post-quantum" security and networking layer is rising to defend against them.

links.name: Who Benefits First
links.what: The industries expected to gain earliest once the machines work — drug discovery, materials, finance and logistics. Illustrative, not pure quantum plays.

members.why: Pharma — molecular simulation for drug discovery (Merck)

robotics.name: Robotics & Automation
robotics.description: The march of the machines — from the sensors, vision and motion parts that make up a robot, through the robot and cobot makers and the factory automation giants, to the AI brains turning pre-programmed arms into machines that perceive and adapt.

links.name: Sensors, Vision & Motion
links.what: The robot's body parts — machine-vision cameras, precision sensors, motors and actuators that let a robot see and move.

links.name: AI Brains & Chips
links.what: The AI models and chips that give robots intelligence — the leap from pre-programmed arms to machines that perceive, learn and adapt.

links.name: Robot & Cobot Makers
links.what: The companies that actually build the robots — from factory arms and collaborative cobots to surgical and delivery robots.

links.name: Factory Automation
links.what: The control systems and industrial giants that automate whole factories and connect the machines together.

links.name: Who Deploys It
links.what: Where robots go to work first — e-commerce warehouses and autonomous farm & construction equipment. Illustrative, not robot pure-plays.

space.name: Space & Defense
space.description: The new space race meets modern defense — from the rockets getting to orbit cheaper than ever and the satellites beaming data back, through the defense primes and the new wave of cheap drones and battlefield AI, down to the specialist suppliers inside almost every mission.

links.name: Launch & Access to Space
links.what: Getting to orbit — the rockets and landers that carry satellites and cargo into space, now cheaper than ever.

links.name: Suppliers & Electronics
links.what: The specialist parts makers inside almost every aircraft, missile and satellite — high-margin, mission-critical components.

links.name: Satellites & Earth Data
links.what: The satellites in orbit and the data they beam back — imaging, connectivity and Earth-observation.

links.name: Drones & Defense Tech
links.what: The new wave of defense — cheap drones, loitering munitions and the AI software that runs modern battlefields.

links.name: Defense Primes
links.what: The big defense contractors — missiles, fighter jets, warships and the space & missile-defense programs behind them.

nuclear.name: Nuclear & Power
nuclear.description: The electricity boom behind the AI datacenter build-out — from the uranium miners and fuel enrichers, through the reactor and small-modular reactor (SMR) builders and the power producers running the fleet, to the grid and electrical equipment straining to keep up.

links.name: Uranium & Fuel
links.what: The nuclear fuel supply chain — the miners digging up uranium and the enrichers that turn it into reactor-grade fuel.

members.why: Cameco — the top Western uranium miner

links.name: Reactors & SMRs
links.what: The companies building the reactors — from small modular reactors (SMRs) to next-gen designs racing to power the AI boom.

links.name: Grid & Electrical Equipment
links.what: The picks-and-shovels of the power build-out — turbines, transformers, switchgear and the datacenter power gear straining to keep up.

links.name: Power Producers
links.what: The utilities and independent power producers that run the nuclear fleet and sell the electricity — the most direct AI-datacenter beneficiaries.

links.name: The Power Hunger
links.what: Why it is all happening — the hyperscalers signing nuclear power deals to feed AI datacenters. Illustrative, not power stocks.

ev.name: EVs & Batteries
ev.description: The electric-vehicle value chain, end to end — from the lithium and rare earths dug out of the ground, through the battery makers and next-gen cell chemistries, to the carmakers, the charging networks and the power semiconductors that manage every electron in an EV.

links.name: Battery Materials
links.what: The raw inputs — lithium, rare earths and the miners & refiners that feed the battery supply chain.

links.name: Battery Makers & Tech
links.what: The cells themselves — and the next-gen chemistries (solid-state, silicon) racing to make EVs cheaper and go farther.

links.name: EV Chips & Power Electronics
links.what: The unsung winners — the power semiconductors and chips that manage every electron in an EV, the biggest jump in chip content autos have ever seen.

links.name: EV Makers
links.what: The carmakers — from EV-only pioneers to the legacy giants betting billions to catch up.

links.name: Charging & Infrastructure
links.what: The plumbing — the charging networks and hardware that have to be built out before mass EV adoption can happen.

cleanenergy.name: Clean Energy: Solar, Wind & Storage
cleanenergy.description: The other side of the energy transition — from the solar-panel makers and the inverters & trackers that wire them up, through the rooftop installers and the battery & fuel-cell storage that fixes the intermittency problem, to the renewable utilities feeding it all onto the grid.

links.name: Solar Manufacturers
links.what: The companies making the panels & modules themselves — a brutal, low-margin business dominated by scale and squeezed by cheap imports.

members.why: First Solar — the US thin-film leader

links.name: Inverters, Trackers & Hardware
links.what: The higher-value electronics around the panel — inverters, trackers and the electrical balance-of-system that turns sunlight into usable power.

links.name: Rooftop Solar & Adoption
links.what: The installers and financiers that put solar on homes and businesses — where consumer adoption actually happens.

links.name: Storage & Fuel Cells
links.what: The fix for renewables' biggest flaw — batteries and fuel cells that store power for when the sun sets and the wind drops.

links.name: Renewable Utilities & IPPs
links.what: The utilities and independent power producers that own the wind & solar farms and sell the clean electricity onto the grid.

minerals.name: Copper & Critical Minerals
minerals.description: The picks-and-shovels of everything electric — copper for the grid, EVs and AI datacenters, plus the rare earths and magnets modern tech cannot work without. From the miners digging it up and the diversified giants, to the royalty financiers that take a cut, to the demand pulling it all.

links.name: Copper Miners
links.what: "Dr. Copper" — the metal behind every wire, motor and datacenter. Pure-play miners are the most direct bet on the electrification super-cycle.

links.name: Diversified Mining Giants
links.what: The global majors that mine copper, iron ore and more at massive scale — steadier, dividend-paying ways to own the commodity boom.

links.name: Rare Earths & Magnets
links.what: The niche metals that go into EV motors, wind turbines and defense systems — where the West is scrambling to break China's grip.

links.name: Royalty & Streaming
links.what: The financiers of mining — they fund mines in exchange for a cut of production, earning miner-like upside with far less operating risk.

links.name: The Metal Hunger
links.what: Why it all matters — the grid build-out, EVs and AI datacenters devouring copper and critical minerals. Illustrative, not miners.

members.why: AI datacenters need vast power & copper (Nvidia)
EVs use ~4x the copper of a car (Tesla)

water.name: Water
water.description: The most essential resource, as an investment theme — the equipment makers that pump, treat and pipe it, the regulated utilities that deliver it to your tap, and the irrigation systems that grow the world's food. A classic defensive way to own scarcity.

links.name: Pumps, Valves & Metering
links.what: Moving and measuring water — the pumps, valves and smart meters that run inside every water system.

links.name: Pipes & Infrastructure
links.what: The physical network — the pipes, drainage and engineering behind fixing America's ageing, leaking water infrastructure.

links.name: Treatment & Filtration
links.what: Making water clean and safe — the chemicals, filtration and quality-testing that treat drinking water and wastewater.

links.name: Water Utilities
links.what: The regulated companies that actually deliver water to homes and businesses — steady, defensive, dividend-paying.

members.why: American Water Works — the US giant

links.name: Irrigation & Ag Water
links.what: The biggest user of all — the irrigation systems that water the world's crops, where scarcity bites hardest.

agriculture.name: Food & Agriculture
agriculture.description: The farm-to-table supply chain and the food-security story behind it — from the seeds, fertilizer and machinery that grow the crop, through animal health and the processors & ingredient makers, to the distributors that get food to the table. Spans materials, industrials, health care and staples.

links.name: Animal Health
links.what: Keeping livestock and pets healthy — vaccines, diagnostics and medicines, a steadier high-margin corner of ag.

links.name: Farm Equipment
links.what: The machines that work the land — tractors, combines and precision-ag tech driving higher output per acre.

links.name: Seeds & Fertilizer
links.what: What goes into the ground — the seeds, crop chemicals and fertilizers that set the yield. A commodity business, and a geopolitical one.

links.name: Processing & Ingredients
links.what: Turning raw crops into food — the grain traders, crushers and ingredient makers in the middle of the chain.

links.name: Food Distribution
links.what: Getting it to the table — the broadline distributors that supply restaurants, cafeterias and grocers.

glp1.name: GLP-1 & Obesity
glp1.description: The weight-loss drug boom, end to end — from the biotech pipeline and the big drug makers, through the manufacturers and injection devices, to the telehealth platforms that deliver it and the "Ozempic effect" rippling across the economy.

links.name: Drug Discovery & Pipeline
links.what: Biotechs racing to build the next generation of obesity drugs — pills instead of injections, and even stronger results.

links.name: The Drug Makers
links.what: The giants behind today's blockbuster weight-loss and diabetes drugs, plus the big pharma challengers trying to catch up.

links.name: Contract Manufacturing
links.what: The specialists that actually make the drug at scale — the biggest bottleneck, since demand has far outstripped supply.

links.name: Injection Devices & Delivery
links.what: The pens, auto-injectors, needles and vials that get the drug into patients.

links.name: Diagnostics & Monitoring
links.what: Continuous glucose monitors and tests used to manage patients on these drugs.

links.name: Telehealth & Access
links.what: The online platforms and pharmacies that prescribe, compound and deliver the drugs to millions of new patients.

links.name: The "Ozempic Effect"
links.what: Second-order impact — as people eat less, it ripples into snacks, drinks, dialysis and other corners of the economy.

members.why: Dialysis — long-term kidney benefit is a headwind (DaVita)

genomics.name: Genomics & Precision Medicine
genomics.description: Medicine rebuilt around DNA — from the machines that read the genome and the tools & reagents behind them, through the gene-editing pioneers rewriting it and the liquid-biopsy tests that catch disease early, to the AI platforms designing tomorrow's drugs.

links.name: Sequencing Platforms
links.what: The machines that read DNA — the foundation of the whole field. As the cost of sequencing a genome collapses, everything downstream gets cheaper.

links.name: Tools & Reagents
links.what: The "picks-and-shovels" of biotech — the instruments, chemicals and lab kits every genomics company buys, whoever wins the science.

links.name: Diagnostics & Liquid Biopsy
links.what: The tests — spotting cancer and disease early from a blood draw. The nearest-term, most commercial slice of genomics.

links.name: Gene Editing & Cell Therapy
links.what: The pioneers actually rewriting DNA — CRISPR and cell therapies chasing one-time cures for genetic disease. High-risk, high-reward.

links.name: AI Drug Discovery
links.what: The new layer — companies using AI and computation to design drugs faster and cheaper than the lab-bench trial-and-error of the past.

aging.name: Aging & Longevity
aging.description: Investing in the demographic megatrend of an aging population — from the treatments and devices that keep people healthy longer, through the vision, hearing and monitoring tech and the senior-living operators, to the insurers and wealth managers funding a longer retirement. Spans health care, real estate and financials.

links.name: Vision, Hearing & Monitoring
links.what: The everyday maintenance of ageing — eye care, contact lenses and the respiratory & monitoring devices used for chronic conditions.

links.name: Medical Devices
links.what: The hardware that repairs an ageing body — replacement joints, heart valves, pacemakers and surgical robots.

links.name: Age-Related Treatments
links.what: The drugs targeting the diseases of ageing — Alzheimer's, cancer, heart and metabolic disease — where an older population means growing demand.

links.name: Senior Living & Care
links.what: Where older people live and are cared for — the senior-housing REITs and the skilled-nursing and assisted-living operators.

links.name: Retirement & Insurance
links.what: The money side of a long life — the life insurers, annuity providers and wealth managers that fund decades of retirement.

housing.name: Housing & Homebuilders
housing.description: The US housing machine, end to end — from the building products that go into a home, through the homebuilders that put them up and the mortgage lenders that finance the buyers, to the retailers where owners renovate and the REITs that rent it all out. A classic rate-cut play.

links.name: Building Products & Materials
links.what: The stuff homes are made of — lumber, insulation, paint, decking and fixtures. Sells into both new builds and renovations.

links.name: Homebuilders
links.what: The companies that actually build and sell new homes — the most direct bet on US housing supply and demand.

links.name: Mortgage & Title
links.what: The money side — the lenders, mortgage insurers and title companies that finance the purchase. Extremely sensitive to interest rates.

links.name: Residential REITs & Rental
links.what: The landlords — companies that own and rent out homes and apartments, an income play on the same housing demand.

links.name: Home Improvement Retail
links.what: Where homeowners spend once they own — the big-box and specialty retailers riding the repair & remodel cycle.

reshoring.name: Reshoring & US Manufacturing
reshoring.description: The multi-year push to rebuild US factory capacity — from the raw materials and the firms that construct the plants, through the automation and electrical gear that outfit them, to the rail and warehousing that moves the output. A policy-driven story cutting across industrials, materials and real estate.

links.name: Materials & Inputs
links.what: The raw stuff of a factory build-out — steel, cement and aggregates. Demand rises with every new plant, highway and grid upgrade.

links.name: Factory & Infra Builders
links.what: The engineering and construction firms that actually put up the fabs, plants and infrastructure — the direct beneficiaries of the capex wave.

links.name: Factory Automation
links.what: The control systems and machines that run a modern factory floor — the productivity layer that makes higher-cost US manufacturing viable.

links.name: Electrical & Power Equipment
links.what: The switchgear, transformers and power gear every new factory and datacenter needs to plug into the grid — a supply bottleneck.

links.name: Logistics & Warehousing
links.what: Moving the output — the railroads, truckers and industrial-property owners that carry and store reshored production.

fintech.name: Fintech & Digital Payments
fintech.description: The digitisation of money — from the card networks that move it, through the processors that plug merchants in and the neobanks & apps that hold it, to the digital lenders and the infrastructure behind the scenes. A convergence of finance and software.

links.name: Card Networks & Rails
links.what: The toll-roads of money — the networks that carry a payment between bank and merchant and take a tiny cut of nearly every swipe.

links.name: Payment Processors
links.what: The plumbing that connects merchants to the networks — handling the transaction, the terminal and the settlement.

links.name: Digital Lending & BNPL
links.what: Credit, reinvented — buy-now-pay-later and data-driven lenders underwriting loans in real time online.

links.name: Neobanks & Apps
links.what: The consumer front-end — app-first banks, brokerages and wallets taking share from the old branch-based incumbents.

links.name: Fintech Infrastructure
links.what: The picks-and-shovels — the credit-scoring, core-banking and cross-border rails every other fintech is built on.

members.why: Fair Isaac — the FICO credit score

crypto.name: Crypto & Blockchain
crypto.description: The public-equity ways to own the crypto economy — from the power-hungry compute that secures the chain and the bitcoin miners, through the exchanges and brokers, to the corporate treasuries and the stablecoin issuers turning blockchain into a payments rail. High-beta, early, and narrow.

links.name: Crypto Compute & Power
links.what: The data-center and power backbone — miners increasingly pivoting their cheap power and racks to AI/HPC as well as crypto.

links.name: Bitcoin Miners
links.what: The companies running the machines that mint new bitcoin — a leveraged, high-beta bet on the coin price and mining economics.

members.why: MARA Holdings — the largest US miner

links.name: Exchanges & Brokers
links.what: Where crypto is traded and held — the exchanges, brokers and trading firms that earn fees on the flow.

links.name: Stablecoins & Payments
links.what: The bridge to real-world money — issuers of dollar-pegged stablecoins turning blockchain into a payments and settlement rail.

links.name: Corporate BTC Treasuries
links.what: Companies that hold bitcoin on the balance sheet as a treasury asset — a leveraged, stock-market proxy for the coin.
